title: Why is the Mona Lisa so famous?
subject: art
description: It is the most famous painting in the world. Yet in 1503, its own painter had better things to do than the portrait of a merchant's wife.

hero.hook: The most looked-at painting on the planet may have been just a side project for Leonardo.

blocks.text: Every day, about 20,000 people file past one small painting in Paris. Most of them look at it for less than a minute. Almost none of them could say why this one, and not another.

blocks.caption: Here she is. Oil on a poplar panel, 77 cm by 53: about the size of a carry-on bag.

stops.text: Here she is. Oil on a poplar panel, 77 cm by 53: about the size of a carry-on bag.
**The smile.** Look at the corners of the mouth: there is no line anywhere. Leonardo blurs them with a technique called [[sfumato]], so the smile seems to change as your eyes move.
**The eyes.** No eyebrows, no eyelashes. They may have faded with time, or been cleaned away. The gaze seems to follow you around the room.
**The hands.** Relaxed, one over the other. At the time, portraits were stiff and cut at the chest. Showing the hands, calm and soft, was new.
**A bridge.** Behind her right shoulder, the only sign of human life in a strange landscape of rocks and water.
A masterpiece, then. But in 1900 it was one masterpiece among many. Something else had to happen.

sections.title: A portrait that was never delivered

blocks.text: Florence, around **1503**. A silk merchant, Francesco del Giocondo, orders a portrait of his wife, Lisa. The painter is the most admired artist in the city: Leonardo da Vinci.

blocks.caption: Leonardo around 1515, drawn by his pupil Francesco Melzi. Painter, engineer, anatomist: he started many things and finished few.

blocks.text: Leonardo works slowly. He never hands the portrait over. He keeps it with him for the rest of his life, adding thin layers of paint year after year.

blocks.prompt: The painting is Italian. So **why is it in Paris** today?
options: Napoleon's army took it from Italy.
Leonardo carried it to France himself.
France bought it from Italy in 1900.
blocks.explanation: Leonardo moved to France at the end of his life and brought the painting with him. The map shows the journey.

blocks.text: Florence. This is where Lisa sits for Leonardo, and where the painting begins. 1516. The French king, Francis I, invites the old painter to his court. Leonardo, aged 64, crosses the Alps with the portrait in his luggage and settles in Amboise. He dies there in 1519. The king keeps the painting. After the French Revolution, the royal collection goes to a new museum in Paris: the Louvre.

steps.text: **Florence.** This is where Lisa sits for Leonardo, and where the painting begins.
**1516.** The French king, Francis I, invites the old painter to his court. Leonardo, aged 64, crosses the Alps with the portrait in his luggage and settles in Amboise.
He dies there in **1519**. The king keeps the painting. After the French Revolution, the royal collection goes to a new museum in Paris: the [[Louvre]].

blocks.text: For four centuries, the portrait is admired by painters and writers. But it is not a star. In the Louvre's own galleries, bigger and more dramatic paintings draw the crowds.

blocks.prompt: In 1900, the Mona Lisa was **already** the most famous painting in the world.
blocks.explanation: It was respected, and well known to art lovers. But most people outside that circle could not have named it. That changed in a single week of 1911.

blocks.text: **Monday, August 21, 1911.** The Louvre is closed for cleaning. A man in a white worker's smock lifts the painting off its hooks, removes it from its frame in a stairwell, and walks out with it under his clothes.

blocks.caption: This photo is taken in the Louvre a few days later.

stops.text: This photo is taken in the Louvre a few days later.
**The gap.** Between two paintings, four iron hooks and nothing else. Nobody notices for more than a day: guards assume the portrait is away being photographed.
Then the news breaks, and something odd happens. People queue for hours to stare at the empty wall.

blocks.text: The theft makes front pages around the world. The police question the young painter Pablo Picasso and jail the poet Guillaume Apollinaire for a week. Both are innocent. For two years, there is no trace of the painting.

blocks.caption: The real thief: Vincenzo Peruggia, an Italian workman. He knew the place well. He had helped build the painting's protective glass case.

blocks.prompt: Where was the painting **hidden** for two years?
options: In a bank vault in Switzerland.
In a trunk in the thief's room in Paris.
blocks.explanation: Peruggia kept it in a trunk with a false bottom, in his small room, a couple of kilometers from the Louvre.

blocks.text: December 1913. Peruggia writes to an art dealer in Florence. He says he wants to bring the Mona Lisa home to Italy, for a reward. He takes the train across the Alps with the painting in his trunk. Four centuries after Leonardo, the portrait makes the journey in reverse. Florence. The dealer checks the back of the panel, recognizes the real thing, and calls the police. Peruggia is arrested in his hotel.

steps.text: **December 1913.** Peruggia writes to an art dealer in Florence. He says he wants to bring the Mona Lisa home to Italy, for a reward.
He takes the train across the Alps with the painting in his trunk. Four centuries after Leonardo, the portrait makes the journey in reverse.
**Florence.** The dealer checks the back of the panel, recognizes the real thing, and calls the police. Peruggia is arrested in his hotel.

blocks.caption: Florence, December 1913. Before going back to Paris, the painting is shown at the Uffizi Gallery. Italians queue to see it.
Paris, the next morning. This paper prints more than a million copies a day.

stops.text: Paris, the next morning. This paper prints more than a million copies a day.
**The headline**: “The Mona Lisa is found.” Her face fills the front page. For two years, newspapers everywhere have printed it again and again.
Millions of people who had never set foot in a museum now know her face. That is the real effect of the theft.

blocks.text: Peruggia claimed he acted out of patriotism, to return the painting to Italy. An Italian court gave him about a year in prison. He served seven months.

sections.title: The most looked-at face on Earth

blocks.text: In **January 1914**, the painting returns to the Louvre. It has never stopped drawing crowds since. Artists copy it, mock it, put it on posters and mugs. Each joke makes it more famous.

blocks.caption: The Louvre, today. This is the room where she hangs.

stops.text: The Louvre, today. This is the room where she hangs.
**There she is.** That small dark rectangle on the far wall, behind bulletproof glass and a barrier.
**And here are her visitors.** Most of them see her through a phone screen, over someone else's shoulder.

blocks.explanation: It took more than a day. The museum was closed, and paintings were often taken down to be photographed. A visiting painter finally asked where she was.

blocks.prompt: Last question. Put the painting's story **in order**.
items: Leonardo starts the portrait in Florence
He carries it across the Alps to France
It is stolen from the Louvre
blocks.explanation: Four quiet centuries, then two years that changed everything.

blocks.text:
The Mona Lisa is a real masterpiece: the blurred smile, the hands and the landscape were all new in their time.
It is in France because Leonardo brought it there himself in 1516.
Its worldwide fame dates from 1911: a theft, two years of headlines, and a face printed millions of times.
